title: CS QBR metrics signal diary — annotated working notes
content:
Audience: CS leads + Solutions Eng. Purpose: a compact but opinionated reference for QBR metric definitions (how we measure), common pitfalls, and a small KPI table to drop into slides. Working — I expect tweaks after the next customer review.

SUMMARY:
- This is intentionally operational (how we compute numbers for customer QBRs) rather than philosophical definitions. Focused metrics: latency (p50/p95/p99), uptime (service-level availability), cost-per-token (hosted billable cost), and cache hit rate (prefix/kv).
- Intended use: one-page appendix for QBR decks + JIRA fields we populate when a metric is flagged.

MEASUREMENT PRINCIPLES (applies to everything):
- Time window: default 30d lookback for trending, 7d for recent momentum. Call out the QBR reporting window explicitly in slides.
- Granularity: compute daily aggregates (per-customer daily), then roll to percentiles/SLAs. Avoid using raw request-level outliers without context.
- Missing data: if telemetry gaps > 3% in window, annotate and exclude that day from SLA calculations.

METRIC DEFINITIONS:
1) Latency (observability name: inference.latency_ms)
   - What: client request -> first-token emitted latency. For streaming routes measure first-byte; for non-streaming measure full-generation latency.
   - Primary numbers we report: p50, p95, p99 (ms) computed per-customer over the chosen window.
   - Measurement details: use server-side timestamps (ingress request received, token emit timestamp). Normalize for network egress in cross-region scenarios (tag requests by region).
   - Example PromQL-ish query (implementation note):
     avg_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_latency_bucket[1d])))[30d:1d])  // approximate
   - Common gotchas: background warmups (cold KV cache) inflate p99 during the first 1–2 hours after deploy. Exclude rollout windows or annotate them.

2) Uptime (observability name: infra.availability_pct)
   - What: percentage of requests that returned a 2xx/allowed success code within the SLA latency cap. We prefer a combined availability+latency SLO (e.g., request counted as success only if returned within 5s).
   - Measurement window: rolling 30d for QBR reporting and 7d for incident follow-ups.
   - Calculation: uptime_pct = 100 * (successful_requests_within_cap / total_valid_requests).
   - Edge cases: synthetic traffic vs real traffic — keep separate; QBR uses real customer traffic only (unless customer has low volume, in which case use synth with note).

3) Cost per token (billing.metric: cost_per_token_usd)
   - What: the incremental hosting cost allocated to a customer divided by billable tokens in the window. This is *not* the invoice line item but a cost allocation used in renewal discussions.
   - Formula: cost_per_token = (gpu_hours_cost + infra_amortized + storage_cost_share + caching infra) / billable_tokens.
   - Notes: amortization and allocation rules must be documented in finance playbook — for QBR use the monthly allocation provided by Finance (tagged per-customer).
   - Example: If allocated infra cost = $9,000 in 30d and billable tokens = 3,000,000 -> $0.003/token.
   - Typical thresholds: flag if > 2x org baseline or trending +25% QoQ without quality gain.

4) Cache hit rate (telemetry name: kv_cache.hit_ratio or prefix_cache.hit_ratio)
   - What: proportion of requests where the prefix or KV lookup prevented full-token computation. We track two flavors: prefix cache (short-context reuse) and KV/persistence cache (longer-term).
   - Formula: hit_rate = hits / (hits + misses). Compute per-route and per-model.
   - Measurement caveats: for streaming workloads a partial hit (some prefix found) should be counted and weighted by tokens saved — we approximate with boolean hit in QBR but note token-saved estimate in comments.
   - Actionable thresholds: aim > 40% prefix hit for high-reuse assistants; < 10% suggests cache config mismatch or prompts too dynamic.

KPI TABLE (drop-in for QBR slide) — columns: Metric | QBR target | Reporting window | How we compute | Owner | Escalation trigger

Metric | QBR target | Reporting window | How we compute | Owner | Escalation trigger
Latency (p95) | <= 800ms | 30d | server-side p95 for first-token | eng-sre | p95 > target for 2 consecutive weeks
Uptime | >= 99.5% | 30d | success within latency cap / total | customer-success + eng-sre | daily < 99.0% or incident >1/week
Cost per token | <= $0.0025 | 30d | allocated-cost / billable_tokens | finance + cs-ops | > 2x baseline or +30% QoQ
Cache hit rate (prefix) | >= 35% | 30d | hits/(hits+misses) per-route | solutions-eng | < 15% for 2 weeks

(footnote: targets above are sample starting points; each enterprise customer may have bespoke targets in contract)

ALERTING / SIGNALS TO SURFACE TO CS:
- Spikes in p95 with stable p50 -> tail events (invest SLO and rollout logs).
- Simultaneous uptick in cost/token and drop in cache hit -> likely cache invalidation or prompts changed.
- Uptime slip with no infra incidents but higher latency -> overload / queuing; consider routing to larger instance type or enabling burst capacity for customer.

SAMPLE SLIDE COPY (short):
"Service reliability: p95 620ms (target <=800ms), uptime 99.7% (target 99.5%). Month-over-month cost/token $0.0021 (-8%) driven by +12% cache hit rate after prompt compacting."

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES (for engineers we link during QBR prep):
- Tag requests with customer_id and route. Ensure model variant is recorded.
- Store per-request metadata: model_id, seq_len, cached_prefix_hit, kv_hit, tokens_generated, latency_ms, response_code.
- Maintain a per-customer telemetry completeness field; exclude windows with <97% telemetry capture.

OPEN QUESTIONS / DECISIONS NEEDED:
- Do we include streaming partial-token latencies differently in aggregated p95? (action: eng-observability to propose normalized rule)
- Finance allocation cadence: use calendar month or trailing-30d for QBRs? (finance to decide)

NEXT STEPS BEFORE NEXT QBR:
- (Ethan) add the per-route prefix vs kv hit table to the QBR appendix (due 2024-12-01).
- (Priya) align cost allocation rule with Finance and add linkage to invoice lines (due 2024-11-20).
- (Noah) draft PromQL and example Grafana panels for p50/p95/p99 and cache hit breakdown (due 2024-11-25).

NOTES TO SELF: keep language simple for exec slide (avoid PromQL), but include appendix with exact queries for SRE/SEs.

Historical: pulled some phrasing from past QBRs for ACME and Nova customers — kept examples anonymized.

End of working notes.
